assumption_register.name: Transfer dwell
assumption_register.source: 48 h from the benchmark page; the 3.5 d wait is a model convention

assumption_register.name: Bunker price
assumption_register.source: benchmark page (600 USD/t); not a market price; fuel grade / fuel systems unverified

assumption_register.source: fleet file carries no fuel-system data

assumption_register.name: Service frequency granularity

assumption_register.source: no source defines the allowed frequencies; paper uses fractional vessels

assumption_register.value: CostPerFULL, CostPerFULLTrnsf are USD per FFE (divided by 2 -> per TEU); port call = fixed + PortCallCostPerFFE x vessel capacity per call

problem_analysis:
Size: Small
Complexity Drivers:
- 47 ports x 1764 lanes -> combinatorial explosion above 2209 route candidates.
- Network density 163.2% across 47 ports increases routing difficulty.
- Total demand 276,494 TEU requires capacity balancing across 0 services.
Demand Concentration: low - top-5 share 5.7% implies mixed hub and direct strategy.
Decomposition Rationale: ~15 ports per region enables scalable 3-agent optimization.

archetype_params.notes: The hybrid archetype is confirmed by the median demand of 98.0 TEU and total volume of 147,894 TEU, supporting a mix of direct services for high-volume lanes and hub routing for the remainder. With a top-3 share of only 7.2%, approximately 80% of the ~800 candidate lanes are expected to be retained via hub-and-spoke or feeder connections rather than direct point-to-point services.

regional_results.strategy:
Strategy: C
Selected: hybrid
Reason 1: Median demand of 98.0 TEU/lane indicates fragmented volume requiring direct service for high-density corridors like CNYTN -> USLAX (3,730 TEU/wk) while maintaining hub consolidation for lower-density lanes.
